input.brief: Title page of a PC-local library of inventions made and tested in a VR lab: one real 3D prototype assembles from its kit parts on a black stage as you scroll, then you go to the invention list, researchers, and messages

direction.name: The object, large
direction.idea: Show the thing, bigger than seems reasonable. One photographed object fills the first screen, scaled until the viewport crops it, with the text small and tucked beside or behind it. The crop is the idea: a record whose edge leaves the top-right corner, a bottle whose shoulder runs off the bottom, a chair seen so close you read its grain. Being that close reads as confidence in the object. Everything else on the page serves it: details as tight close-ups, facts as short lines, one way to buy.
direction.composition: First screen: the object occupies 55–75% of the viewport and breaks at least one edge. It sits on a flat field (ground colour or one bold colour), never in a box. The headline is short and either very large and partly hidden behind the object (10–13vw, the object overlapping two or three letters) or small (28–36px) in the opposite corner with a one-line description. No navigation bar beyond a wordmark and one action. Following sections: a row of three or four close-up details at different crop ratios (not equal tiles), a single wide photograph of the object in use, a plain list of facts set large (materials, size, price) aligned to one edge, then the purchase action. The object returns once at the end from a different angle.
direction.typography: Either very large and structural or very small and precise; pick one for the headline and hold it. Facts are set in the text face at 22–28px, not in a table.
direction.colour: A flat field chosen to make the object's own colour sing (its complement, or a tone darker than its shadow side). One field for the whole page, or a second for the facts section.
direction.imagery: Use the product's own photographs if they exist. Otherwise use a still-life from the dealt set as a stand-in and say so. Prefer images with a plain background; use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` on light fields so a white studio background disappears into the page colour.
direction.photoTreatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.
direction.richness: The object's surface at close range, and the tension of the crop.
direction.pitfalls: A small centred product shot with space all round is a catalogue thumbnail, not this direction. If the image has a busy background it cannot sit on a field; crop tighter or change image. Keep text off the object's focal area.

hero.name: Object on the seam
hero.blueprint: A white or very pale page organised by one change of tone. A square-cornered panel one step darker than the page (a flat pale blue-grey or warm grey) fills the top 44% of the viewport inside 12px margins; the page colour runs below it. The object, photographed on a plain background and blended with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, straddles the seam between the two tones: it is about 62% of the viewport wide, starts at column 6 and runs off the right edge, with its upper half over the panel and its lower half over the page. Type is small and exact. The headline is two lines at 24px in medium weight, far left on columns 1–3 at a 32px margin, its first baseline resting exactly on the seam; the second line is set in the softer ink. One supporting sentence at 15px, max 34ch, sits 120px lower on the same margin with the single action as a small rectangular button under it. A plain top row inside the panel at 14px: wordmark left, three text links centred, one text link right.
hero.mobile: The tonal panel takes the top 46svh. The object is 120vw wide, centred on the seam and cropped by the right edge. The headline sits just under the seam at 22px on two lines at a 20px margin, with the sentence at 15px beneath and then the button. The wordmark sits top-left inside the panel; the links collapse to one word top-right.
hero.headline: Two short sentences at 24px, one per line and up to about 28 characters each, the second in the softer ink.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors
photos.treatment: Scale the main image well past its container (`width: 120–160%`) and let `overflow: hidden` on the section do the cropping.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Narrow column, empty field
sections.blueprint: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top. It holds four or five short paragraphs at 15–16px with leading 1.5 and one blank line between them; the first paragraph is in medium weight and full ink, the rest in regular weight and the soft ink. No heading, no image, no button; one underlined text link may end the last paragraph. The remaining three-quarters of the 1440 screen is untouched ground, and the section is only as tall as the text plus 160px of padding below. The column's left edge must match a line used elsewhere on the page (the wordmark's left edge or a later column). Where the page has a large object or a fixed photograph, this column is the small text beside it. Holds 90–150 words comfortably.
sections.mobile: The column becomes 78% of the width, left-aligned at the 20px margin, so a strip of empty ground remains on the right as a deliberate margin. Text stays at 15–16px with the first paragraph in medium weight. Padding is 72px above and 96px below.

sections.name: One frame, three distances
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300vh tall holds a sticky stage of 100svh. On the stage one frame is centred: 30vw wide at 4:5, square corners, overflow hidden. Inside it the same photograph is shown at three distances as the reader scrolls: the whole subject, then scaled to 180% toward one detail, then to 320% on a second detail (transform: scale with a transform-origin per stage, 700ms ease, switched by IntersectionObserver on three invisible markers). The sentence is delivered in halves: its first two or three words sit above the frame at clamp(56px, 8vw, 130px), centred; the last words arrive below the frame at the second stage, overlapping the frame's bottom edge by 0.3em. At the third stage one caption of 28ch at 17px appears to the right of the frame, top-aligned. The two halves together are the heading and stay within two lines.
sections.mobile: The frame grows to 70vw at 4:5 and stays sticky at centre. The first half of the sentence sits above it at 13vw, the second half below it at the same size. The third-stage caption appears under the sentence at 16px, centred.

sections.name: Tiles that grow
sections.blueprint: Order is carried by size. Three flat colour tiles stand in one row, bottom-aligned (align-items: end) with 10px gaps, each larger than the one before: columns 1–3 at 30vh tall, columns 4–7 at 44vh, columns 8–12 at 60vh. Each tile holds one photograph of the subject at that stage (raw, in progress, finished), centred and scaled so the object grows from tile to tile; on light tiles mix-blend-mode: multiply removes a white studio background. One palette colour per tile. Text sits under the tiles, outside them, aligned to each tile's left edge: a stage name at 20px medium whose wording carries the order ('Picked', 'Pressed', 'Poured') and two lines at 16px in the soft ink. The heading, two to four words at 40–52px, occupies the empty ground above the two smaller tiles, top-aligned with the tallest tile. A fourth stage is possible with spans of 2, 3, 3 and 4 columns.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack in order and grow in height instead: 34vw, 46vw and 62vw tall, each at full width. The name and text sit under each tile at 18px and 16px. The heading comes first at 30px. 28px between stages.

sections.name: Sticky photograph, active list
sections.blueprint: Two columns. The left, columns 1–5, is `position: sticky; top: 12vh` and holds one photograph or object at 4:5, 34vw wide, unframed on the ground. The right, columns 7–11, holds a vertical list of five to nine names (treatments, rooms, courses, services) at clamp(20px, 1.6vw, 24px), each row 58px tall with the name at the left and a price or duration right-aligned at 15px in the soft ink. The active row is full ink; the others rest at 40% opacity. Hovering, focusing or scrolling a row to the middle of the viewport makes it active, crossfades the left photograph to that item's image over 300ms, and opens a three-line description at 15px, 34ch wide, directly under the name, pushing later rows down. A heading of two or three words at clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 48px) sits above the list, aligned to its left edge, 48px above the first row.
sections.mobile: The photograph becomes a 4:3 band pinned to the top of the screen at 38svh while the list scrolls beneath it; the heading sits above the first row. Rows are 56px tall and the description opens on tap. The image changes with the row nearest the band.

sections.name: The object returns
sections.blueprint: The thing shown in the hero comes back once, from another angle, to close the page. On one flat field 90svh tall, the object's photograph occupies columns 1–8, scaled to about 130% of that area and anchored so the section's bottom and left edges crop it (`overflow: hidden` on the section; on light fields `mix-blend-mode: multiply` removes a white studio background). The text sits small in columns 10–12, vertically centred: a closing line of three to five words at 32–40px, one sentence at 17px, the price or key fact on its own line at 22px, and one rectangular button. Nothing overlaps the object's focal area. Where the page's subject is a shape rather than a photograph, the page's motif takes the object's place at the same scale as a flat filled shape. The closing line is the only heading.
sections.mobile: The text block comes first: closing line at 28px, sentence, fact, full-width button. The object follows at 130% of the screen width, shifted so the right and bottom edges crop it, filling about 55svh on the same flat field.

sections.name: The back of the card
sections.blueprint: The footer is the reverse side of the page's artefact, laid out as the back of a postcard. A paper-coloured panel spans columns 2–11 on the contrasting ground, about 420px tall, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops (an inline SVG path or `clip-path`, each scallop about 100px wide). The panel is divided by space into two halves. Left half: a short sign-off of two to four words at 32px, then two or three lines at 16px, written like a message. Right half: the address block, four left-aligned lines at 18px with 12px between them, each line a link (email, telephone, street, social); above it in the top-right corner, a stamp: one small photograph, 3:4 and 88px wide, with a 6px paper-coloured margin. Along the panel's bottom edge, a single centred line at 12px gives the copyright like a printer's imprint.
sections.mobile: The panel runs full width with six scallops across its top edge. The stamp sits top-right at 64px wide; the sign-off and message come first, then the address lines at 17px beneath them, then the imprint line centred at 12px.

references.name: Moto Finance
references.idea: A metal card presented like a museum piece: lit by a single overhead light box in a black room, then orbiting through dim architectural stills.
references.hero: Black full-bleed 3D scene. A pale silver-lavender light panel, a trapezoid in perspective like a ceiling light box, occupies the top 20% and centre 55% of the viewport. The two-line uppercase headline, centred at 4.4vw in medium grotesk with tight leading, straddles the panel's lower edge so its first line sits half on light, half on black. In the exact centre a small metal card stands on a low plinth, only about 150px wide, surrounded by darkness. A light-grey pill button (about 250 by 52px) is centred near the bottom; the logo is top-left and a dark pill button top-right.
references.type: Neue Montreal only: weight 500 uppercase at 64px (4.4vw) with near-zero tracking and leading under 1.0 for headings, 20px sentence case for body, tiny caps labels in the footer. Three sizes; centred until the left-aligned footer.
references.colour: #080808 #edefef #c4cbd6 #e1e5e5 #2a2f3a — Black with cool silver-grey and no brand colour at all. One section inverts to pale grey-white with grey type; the only chroma is amber city lights and a blue atmosphere rim on the globe.
references.imagery: Rendered chrome card with an embossed profile medallion, a night-side Earth, and small dim architectural and fashion stills floating as tilted panels in 3D. Everything underexposed, cool and low-saturation.
references.layout: Full-viewport scenes stacked one per screen, each with a centred uppercase heading, an optional short sub-line and a pill button. One light interlude breaks the black. The footer switches to a left-aligned statement with link columns at the far right.

sections.description: Centred heading at the top with a two-line grey sub-line and a pale pill button directly under it. The lower 45% is the top arc of a night-side Earth rising from the bottom edge, about 75% of the viewport wide, with city lights and a bright blue-white rim on the upper right. Three small dark capsule labels with check icons float over and beside the globe at staggered positions, like status notifications.

A dark 3D room: about twelve small photo panels (roughly 70 by 90px, each tilted at its own angle, heavily dimmed) arranged in two loose rows across the full width, receding with blur. The card stands edge-on in the centre, much larger, catching a specular highlight. Later the card faces front at top-centre and a centred two-line heading with a pill button sits under it.

A pale grey-white band. Two tall columns of currency amounts in mid-size light-grey sans, one at a quarter and one at three-quarters of the width, each fading to white at top and bottom like slot-machine reels, with the centre rows darkest. Between them, three short centred lines of small black text. The bottom edge of the band reveals a dark photograph.

steal: Let a headline straddle the edge of a light shape so one line is half on light and half on dark.
Show the product very small in a large dark space in the first viewport, then let it grow as the page scrolls.
Use vertically scrolling columns of real-looking figures, faded at both ends, as a quiet backdrop for a three-line statement.
references.media: An 11s hero video of a CG metal card on a plinth covers the whole first screen and holds on its last frame. Then a pinned WebGL globe in the lower half under centred text, a 3D card centred in a depth cloud of small photo tiles dimmed to 30-40%, full-bleed sticky photographs with text docked in opposite corners, and a photo strip sitting on an index list; all low-key and desaturated, photos meeting the near-black ground through 200-300px fades, 0px radius.
references.motion: The intro ends in about 1.2s as the camera pushes in and the headline, nav and button arrive (load 9.9s), and Lenis then runs 32 ScrollTriggers: the globe pins for 2.5 viewports at scrub 1, the card turns in 3D across its section, the theme inverts to pale grey with the nav colour following, and benefit rows scrub in one by one. Lines rise by yPercent over 0.65s power3.out and leave over 0.45s power2.in, and headings rise from a blur over 1s power2.inOut.

references.name: The Watch
references.idea: A single 3D watch is the only actor: it holds centre stage and turns, flips and finally explodes into parts while giant product-name letters slide behind and in front of it.
references.hero: Light grey field with soft darker blurs toward the corners. A steel chronograph rendered in 3D stands upright at dead centre, about 80% of viewport height. Behind it the product name is set once across the full width in a wide, squared geometric sans at 24vw in mid-grey; the watch covers the middle character, so only two letters at the left edge and two at the right are readable. A thin circle about 700px across with faint radial spokes and one darker arc sits behind the watch like a dial diagram. No navigation, logo, body copy or button anywhere.
references.type: Nekst, a wide squared geometric sans, regular weight, uppercase, used only huge (up to 25vw) in black, mid-grey and white within one line stack. Body is Inter at 12px in 130px columns, roughly a 30x jump with nothing in between.
references.colour: #e8e8e8 #c7c7c7 #a1a1a1 #6b6b6b #0a0a0a #ffffff — Entirely greyscale: pale grey ground with out-of-focus darker clouds, type in black, grey and white. The page darkens to mid-grey for the exploded view. Only the brass gear train adds warmth.
references.imagery: One real-time 3D steel watch shown front, three-quarter, caseback and exploded into dial, movement and plates lined up on a horizontal axis. No photographs; the object floats with no ground shadow.
references.layout: No grid chrome at all: the object holds the centre while type moves around it. Giant letters crop at any edge, captions sit in a 130px column left or right of the watch, and one product label is rotated 90 degrees.

sections.description: Four stacked lines of uppercase display type about 110px tall, flush left at mid-page and running off the right edge: line one mid-grey, line two black, lines three and four pale grey to white. The watch, tilted three-quarter, floats over the upper right of the stack and hides parts of letters, so type and object share the same space instead of sitting side by side.

The watch is turned to show its open caseback, placed just left of centre. To its right, a 130px-wide column holds two micro-paragraphs at 12px, each with a grey one-line title above. A small grey circular toggle sits far left. A white display word crops off the top edge. The rest of the frame is empty grey with a darker blurred cloud at upper right.

Exploded view. The ground shifts to a mid-grey vertical gradient with a faint horizon line. The watch's components (dial, tourbillon, movement, barrel, bridges) are separated and spaced along one horizontal axis at eye level like specimens. Tiny part names are set vertically along the bottom edge under each piece; a small prompt with a plus icon sits top-centre.

steal: Set the product name so large that the product itself replaces one of its characters, leaving the name half-hidden and the object as the missing letter.
Stack one display line in three tints (black, mid-grey, white) on a grey ground so a single typeface produces depth without colour.
End a product story with an exploded view laid out on one horizontal axis with vertical micro-labels instead of a spec table.
references.media: One fixed full-bleed WebGL canvas renders every picture: a steel chronograph about 620px tall (69% of the height, 29% of the width) centred inside a 720px ring with the giant model code behind it, then the watch from every side, an exploded line of parts on an axis with leader labels, particle ribbons on black, a black-finish reprise and a close-up cropped by the bottom edge. No photographs and no video; two very tall gradient overlays hand the ground from light to dark and back.
references.motion: The preloader holds at least 4.5s on the 3D assets, then its 720px circle stays to become the ring round the watch while a dark arc draws clockwise over 1.2s. Lenis drives one pinned, scrubbed timeline over 38 screens: the watch turns, separates into parts, the ground moves from #ebebeb to #a1a1a1 to #0a0a0a, and headline lines change colour by their distance from the viewport centre; per-character transforms are written every frame, smoothed by a 20ms ease-out.

references.name: Trevor Noah
references.idea: The comedian as a paper cut-out sticker: his head is torn open and the things he makes (stand-up, books, video) spill out and become the navigation.
references.hero: The desktop capture caught a blank navy frame before the canvas painted; the next frame and the mobile shot show the scene. A deep navy field. The name runs across the top in bold pink grotesk on one line, sized to nearly touch both edges. Centred below is a photographic cut-out of the face with a thick white sticker outline and a torn top edge, from which glossy 3D objects (microphone, book, video player, brain, heart) erupt. Circular arrow buttons sit at the left and right edges; a torn-paper white label beneath the face names the current category. A hairline, a text ticker and a pink pill close the bottom.
references.type: Die Grotesk D bold for the wordmark (361px in the digest), Die Grotesk C for everything else with body near 19px. Tight tracking, title case. Statements run at about 4vw and emphasise words by switching them to pink, never by changing weight or face.
references.colour: #1d2440 #f78fb3 #f6f7ee #2b2b2b — One navy field for the entire page. Pink marks the wordmark, emphasised words and one pill; cream-white fills buttons and paper shapes. Photos bring the only other colour.
references.imagery: Photo cut-outs of the face with thick white die-cut outlines and torn edges, toy-like 3D objects, and small stage photos shaped as peeling stickers or rounded tiles, tilted a few degrees and loosely clustered.
references.layout: Centred, one idea per screen on an unbroken navy ground: statement, section title with drifting objects, a lone pill button. The fixed header has the pink name left and two cream pills right. Elements enter from the edges and overlap instead of sitting in columns.

sections.description: A centred four-line statement in white at about 4vw, the lines stepped and ragged instead of squared off, with one long word in pink on the first line. It occupies the lower half of the viewport while the upper half stays empty navy, and appears to build line by line.

A two-line centred title, first line white and second pink, at about 2.5vw. Beneath it a loose cluster of tilted objects rises from the bottom edge: a 3D video-player tile in the middle, small rounded photo tiles and a 3D microphone to its left, all overlapping. On the next screen the objects have drifted upward past a single cream pill button centred in empty space.

Split footer. Left half: a second, larger cut-out of the face, tilted and cropped by the left and bottom edges, with a small white speech bubble above it. Right half: a five-row menu, each row a tiny index number at left and a bold label at about 2.5vw, separated by hairlines. Legal text is tiny along the bottom.

steal: Cut the subject out of a photo with a thick white sticker border and a torn edge so photography behaves like illustration.
Emphasise words in a statement by colour alone (pink within white) while keeping one face and one weight.
Turn the footer into a large numbered menu beside a cropped portrait whose speech bubble addresses the departing visitor.
references.media: Media covers essentially the whole first screen: a fixed WebGL layer behind everything, a photographic cut-out of the face with a torn top taking about a third of the width and the bottom two thirds of the height, props bursting out of it over the wordmark. Later the props re-form into a collage of tilted sticker photos round a 3D object and a stack of books, torn-paper strips mark the colour changes, and a giant cropped portrait peeks from the footer corner, every photo an alpha cut-out with an 8-10px white sticker outline and no video anywhere.
references.motion: A load of about 7.3s plays as a large counter to 100, the intact face sticker, the crown tearing away, props spilling out and the name last, and Lenis then drives the fixed WebGL stage as the props fly down and re-form per chapter, the ground changing navy, charcoal, navy at torn-paper dividers. Headline lines rise from translateY(120%) through a clip-path over 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1) and stickers pop in from scale 0 on an overshoot curve the house layer does not use, while 11 reduced-motion rules zero every duration.
